title: Moderated AI Development Workflow (MOD-W)
summary: MOD-W is a human-in-the-loop methodology for AI-assisted software development. It separates product, technical, implementation, and QA responsibilities across documented, Moderator-approved Steps.
problem: AI-assisted development can produce opaque code dumps, lost context, weak validation, and blurred responsibility when no one owns the process end to end. MOD-W exists to keep a human Moderator in control of scope, review, and acceptance at every step.
coreIdea: Work moves through role separation, small documented Steps, review gates, and cross-validation before a human Moderator approves it — viable coding, not vibe coding.

principles.title: Role separation
principles.summary: Product, Tech Lead, Development Team, and QA responsibilities stay distinct throughout the workflow.

principles.title: Document-centered steps
principles.summary: Work is defined and reviewed through explicit documents and small, approved Steps.

principles.title: Human moderation
principles.summary: A human Moderator holds final authority over scope, approval, and direction.

principles.title: Review and validation
principles.summary: Implementation goes through Tech Lead review and QA validation before acceptance.

roles.label: Moderator
roles.responsibility: Holds final authority over scope, approval, and direction.

roles.label: Product Owner
roles.responsibility: Owns product intent and acceptance validation.

roles.label: Tech Lead
roles.responsibility: Owns architecture, roadmap, and Step-level technical review.

roles.label: Development Team
roles.responsibility: Implements approved Steps with minimal, scoped changes.

roles.label: QA / Tester
roles.responsibility: Validates completed Steps against their acceptance checks.
